The most compelling feature is the presence of a very large necrotic core, with an `NCR Volume (mL)` of 26.148 and a `Proportion Necrosis` of 30.31%. Extensive necrosis is a cardinal feature of glioblastoma, which is overwhelmingly IDH-wildtype. Furthermore, the absence of a T2-FLAIR mismatch (`T2-FLAIR Mismatch Present`: 0.0) argues against the most common type of IDH-mutant glioma, astrocytoma. The deep gray matter involvement (`Anatomical Overlap Regions` including caudate and putamen) is also more common in IDH-wildtype tumors. Weighing the evidence, the massive necrosis is a much stronger predictor than the tumor's sharp borders, leading to a prediction of IDH-wildtype.

This single feature strongly opposes a codeleted status. Given this profound conflict between classic morphology (sharp borders) and a key high-grade feature (necrosis), the prediction is uncertain.
